messages:
alex: heads-up — saw a small routing feedback loop this morning where cross-region fallback + immediate eviction caused repeat redirects for a handful of tiered customers :thinking_face:
maya: ugh. which flow? dedicated -> aux region fallbacks?
alex: yeah. customer pinned to eu-west, aux in us-west tried to take traffic, then our variant fallback flipped model variant, then they got routed back -> repeat. latency+quota spikes.
simon: sounds like no drain window. we currently evict active sessions immediately when capacity is exceeded.
maya: can we do a graceful drain window (like 60–120s) so in-flight requests finish and new ones are routed to fallback only after drain ends?
taylor: +1. also add max_redirects=1 on the routing policy so we don't bounce between regions in one request path.
jackie: telemetry ask: we need a metric for "redirect_churn" per customer + stack traces of why variant changed (model_version_changes). can we surface that in console?
simon: agree on metrics. quick mitigation: set policy override for affected customers to force origin region until we roll the policy.
alex: proposing config patch:

```
{
  "policy": "tiered-routing",
  "graceful_drain_seconds": 90,
  "max_region_redirects": 1,
  "preserve_kv_cache_on_redirect": true
}
```

maya: preserve_kv_cache_on_redirect is key — otherwise model variant flip forces cold KV and long tails.
taylor: behavior question — if preserve_kv_cache=true, are we OK with cross-region cache transfer semantics? might need TTL clamp.
jackie: add TTL clamp 30s on cache-sync so we avoid stale keys being used in long sessions.
simon: operational playbook: 1) patch routing policy with drain + max_redirects, 2) pin affected customers, 3) push dashboard tile for redirect_churn + model_variant_flip rate, 4) run canary for 1 hour.
alex: I'll open the patch PR and request canary rollout.

deploy-bot: policy patch PR #482 created by alex — CI green.

alex: rolling to canary (10% traffic for eu-west) now. will monitor redirect_churn and p99 latency.

maya: if we still see churn after drain=90s, fallback to circuit-breaker: reject to aux instead of redirect, that avoids loops.
taylor: note for console UX: show "drain state" in rollout UI and allow one-click pin to origin. saves manual policy overrides.
jackie: logged dashboards ticket: MON-312 — add redirect_churn, variant_flip_rate, kv_cache_miss_after_redirect.
simon: can we also limit autoscale-triggered evictions during rollout window? that was part of sequence.
alex: yes, add autoscale cooldown=120s during canary to avoid scale thrash.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to 10% for eu-west at 1842008110.

alex: initial 15m look — redirect_churn down ~82%, p99 latency stable. leaving canary open for 1h. will follow up with docs to eng-runbooks. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — good catch. once we merge we should backfill the routing test to simulate variant flip + redirect and assert no-loop.
simon: adding test to e2e: routing-fallback-safety.
jackie: FYI notified CS about temporary pin for two impacted customers. they acknowledged.

alex: closing loop: plan = merge -> roll to 100% after 1h canary if metrics stable -> add console UX followups + telemetry tickets.

maya: perfect.

simon: careful: add changelog note for "graceful drain" so ops knows the semantics changed.

alex: will do.
